question.leadin: This battle saw the death of Joseph Warren.
question.text: Name this Revolutionary War battle fought near Boston, mostly on nearby Breed's Hill.
question.answerHtml: Battle of Bunker Hill [accept Battle of Breed’s Hill before mentioned]
question.clue: Men killed during this battle included a physician from the Committee of Correspondence, Joseph Warren, who appears in the painting of this battle by John Trumbull.

swap.leadin: This man's British contact, Major Andre, was executed after this man's treason was discovered.
swap.text: Name this traitorous Revolutionary War general, who attempted to surrender West Point to the British.
swap.clue: Along with Ethan Allen, this man captured fort Ticonderoga.

question.leadin: Answer the following about women in early American history.
question.text: This possibly-legendary woman took her husband's place loading cannons at the Battle of Monmouth during the American Revolution. Her nickname comes from her previous role as a water carrier.
question.answerHtml: Molly Pitcher [or Mary Ludwig Hayes McCauley; or Mary Ludwig Hayes McCauley]
question.clue: While fetching water for the troops during the 1778 Battle of Monmouth, this New Jersey woman legendarily took the place of her fallen husband in an artillery crew.

swap.text: Attucks was the first person killed in this event on March 5, 1770. Paul Revere made an engraving showing this event, in which five colonists died in Massachusetts' capital.
swap.clue: Henry Pelham created a depiction of this event which was then copied and attributed to Paul Revere.

question.leadin: Answer the following about women to whom Vice Presidents were married.
question.text: This wife of the first Vice President told her husband John to "remember the ladies" while he was at the Continental Congress. This woman was also an outspoken anti-slavery advocate.
question.clue: This person wrote another letter asking to "remember the ladies and be more generous and favorable to them than your ancestors."

swap.leadin: Answer the following questions about some famous lines in American naval history.
swap.text: During the American Revolution, this "Father of the American Navy" famously stated "I have not yet begun to fight" when asked to surrender by the HMS Serapis, which he captured later in the battle.
swap.clue: He obtained a reputation for cruelty after flogging the carpenter Mungo Maxwell and running-through the leader of a mutiny, causing him to change his name after fleeing Tobago in 1773.

question.text: This general of the Continental Army led a miscalculated assault against the British during the battle, the failure of which led to him being court-martialed.
question.clue: This man wrote numerous letters to Congress during the New York campaign, seeking to replace his superior, George Washington.

swap.leadin: This man was the only Founding Father to sign the First Continental Congress's Continental Association, the Declaration of Independence, the Articles of Confederation, and the Constitution.
swap.text: Name this Connecticut representative at the Constitutional Convention, more famous for brokering the Great Compromise between the Virginia and New Jersey Plans, which created the bicameral legislature.
swap.clue: This author of A Caveat Against Injustice was the only person to sign all four of the Continental Association, the Declaration of Independence, the Articles of Confederation, and the Constitution.

question.text: The Second Quartering Act was part of this set of laws that Thomas Gage oversaw, which also included the Port Act.
question.clue: Following the passage of these laws, Thomas Hutchinson was replaced byThomas Gage as one colony's governor.

swap.leadin: This stronghold was captured by the Green Mountain Boys before Arthur St. Clair ordered its evacuation two years later, in 1777.
swap.text: Name this American fortress of the Revolutionary War, located near Lake Champlain.
swap.clue: This fort's location near Lake Champlain made it useful in monitoring trade routes between New York and Canada.

question.text: One member of this family served as royal governor of New Jersey and was a key Loyalist leader during the Revolution. His father served the patriot cause as a minister to France and earlier published Poor Richard's Almanack.
question.clue: This family, another member of which wrote articles for the New-England Courant under the pseudonym "Silence Dogood" and would go on to begin publishing the The Pennsylvania Gazette in 1728.

swap.leadin: Identify the following about a Revolutionary War battle.
swap.text: This British commander-in-chief and governor of remarked after the Red Coats' three charges up , "One more victory like that will destroy us."
swap.clue: This British general's wife Margaret may have leaked his plans for a secret night march to capture Samuel Adams and John Hancock at Lexington. William Howe replaced this general after the Battle of Bunker Hill.

question.leadin: While serving as the Continental Congress's envoy to France, Silas Deane used a type of this substance containing glycerine and cobalt chloride.
question.text: Name this substance used by a group whose leader Benjamin Tallmadge used the alias "John Bolton." James Jay invented a type of this substance known as the "sympathetic stain."
question.answerHtml: invisible ink [accept security ink; accept sympathetic ink; prompt on ink]

swap.leadin: Accused of being a loyalist for voting against the Declaration of Independence, he quickly silenced doubters with his "Declaration...Setting Forth the Causes and Necessities of their Taking Up Arms"
swap.text: Name this "Penman of the Revolution" whose wrote a series of letters defending the Constitution under the name Fabius.
swap.clue: Along with Thomas McKean, he was one of the two members of the Continental Congress to enter the military, and he opposed John Adams in the Continental Congress by voting against the Declaration of Independence.

question.leadin: This group led an unsuccessful 1775 attempt to capture Montreal in the Battle of Longue-Pointe ("long-pwant").
question.text: Name this group that carried out vigilante violence against New York surveyors whom they called "Yorkers." This group is better known for forcing William Delaplace to surrender cannons that were used to break the defenses of Boston.
question.clue: Fort Crown Point was taken by this militia in the leadup to the capture of Fort Ticonderoga.

swap.text: This battle was won by Daniel Morgan's use of deep lines and lasted only one hour. It secured South Carolina for the Continental Army.
swap.clue: Colonial soldiers in the first two lines of this battle were ordered by Daniel Morgan to fire at British officers before falling back, which made Banastre Tarleton think they were retreating.

question.leadin: This man sentenced a privateer named Joshua Huddy to death after he was captured by Loyalist Forces during the so-called Asgill Affair.
question.text: Name this last colonial governor of New Jersey, who was imprisoned during the American Revolution and then exiled to England. He backed Loyalist guerilla groups like John Bacon's Pine Robbers.
question.answerHtml: William Franklin [prompt on Franklin; do not accept “William Temple Franklin”]
question.clue: During the Revolutionary War, he ordered raids on his former colony as a member of the Refugee Club and presided over the Board of Associated Loyalists in New York, in which position, he ordered the execution of Joshua Huddy in the "Asgill Affair".

swap.leadin: In May of 1776, this man became the frst colonial diplomat to a foreign country when he served as the frst envoy to France, but in December, he was joined by Arthur Lee and Ben Franklin.
swap.text: Name this Connecticut Representative who was later fngered by Arthur Lee as a loyalist spy, and may have been assassi-nated by Edward Bancrof.
swap.clue: In 1776 this man was sent as the colonial representative to France, and convinced Lafayette to fight for the colonial cause. That same year he was joined by Benjamin Franklin and Arthur Lee and the three negotiated a formal treaty of alliance with France in 1778.

question.leadin: In this battle, the Comte de Grasse's 24 ship west Indies fleet was reinforced after 3 indecisive days with siege guns fron Newport.
question.text: Name this battle, named the "decisive battle of the war" by Sir William James, lost by Admiral Thomas Graves.

swap.leadin: As of September 2017, Mark Meckler's COS group has secured support from 12 state legislatures for one of these events centered on a balanced budget amendment.
swap.text: Identify these events that can happen with approval from two-thirds of state legislatures according to Article V of the Constitution. There hasn't been one of these events since 1787.
swap.clue: One of the oldest attendees was the oddly named Daniel of St. Thomas Jenifer, while another attendee, James Wilson, developed an infamous proposal.
